extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, researchers, and practitioners interested in recommender systems, personalized search, and social media algorithm design/impacts
extracted.subtask_description: A high-level explanatory summary of algorithmic curation: the filter approaches, technologies, and social impacts of using recommender systems and personalized search to select online media for users. Covers methods (collaborative/content-based), signal types, AI techniques, and consequences like echo chambers and visibility concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of algorithmic curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic curation is the selection of online media by technologies such as recommender systems and personalized search; curation entails the selective sharing of online content and recommendations based on inferred interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the purpose/goal: selecting content for users by inferring interests. Use this as the baseline criterion when evaluating any system labelled as 'curation'—does it select content programmatically and base choices on inferred user interests?

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative filtering (CF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative filtering methods create recommendations based on a person's usage patterns; CF predicts a person's preference for an item by matching their interests with those of users who have similar interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics and guidance: CF shares ratings between similar users, is based on human behaviour patterns rather than analysis of the content itself, and can apply across text, images, music, and other content types. Evaluate CF systems by how well they match users to similar profiles and leverage communal ratings; consider strengths (captures complex taste attributes) and weaknesses (cold-start problems, popularity bias).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content-based filtering (CBF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content-based filtering builds a user profile to represent the types of items a user has engaged with, based on keywords and attributes used to describe those items; recommendations present items similar to those the user previously engaged with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation notes: CBF constructs item profiles from discrete attributes and a weighted feature vector for the user, with weights computed by classifiers, clustering, decision trees, or neural networks. Evaluate by the fidelity of item metadata/features, weight estimation accuracy, and tendency to over-personalize (narrow recommendations). Example application: Pandora Radio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender systems — use of implicit and explicit signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommender systems rank and suggest content to users based on a combination of implicit and explicit user input. Implicit signals include time spent viewing or engaging; explicit signals include likes, saving pages, reading articles, or sharing content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a recommender, inventory which implicit/explicit signals it uses, how signals are weighted, and whether implicit signals (e.g., dwell time) might be noisy or manipulable. Consider transparency and user control over which signals are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized search — contextualization and user filters
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized search aims to retrieve results most relevant to the user by incorporating contextual factors beyond the explicit query, such as past queries, browsing history, and inferred interests; it may allow users to block content containing certain phrases or hashtags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation points: how context is incorporated, privacy implications of using history, support for explicit user filters/controls, and fallback strategies for users with little/no history (e.g., using content-based filtering for first-time users).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI and machine learning techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Platforms have shifted toward machine-learning and AI-driven approaches (deep learning, reinforcement learning) that allow feeds to be personalized at larger scale and with greater responsiveness to user behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should consider model family (e.g., deep nets, RL), training data scope and biases (outputs are shaped by patterns present in the training data), responsiveness to behaviour changes, computational scale, and risks introduced by opaque models (e.g., difficulty of explanation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information-overload mitigation via ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Early ranking algorithms addressed information overload by surfacing the most recent or most popular posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/evaluation criterion: does the algorithm prioritize recency or popularity to reduce overload? Consider trade-offs: recency favors timeliness; popularity can surface widely valued content but risks reinforcing trends and popularity bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement-optimizing ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Later systems shifted toward ranking content based on predicted engagement, aiming to increase the time users spend on a platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key evaluation factors: objective functions (engagement metrics) and the incentives they create. Note documented side effects: optimising for user interaction can increase the spread of misinformation and contribute to political polarization. Examine whether systems balance engagement with other quality or safety objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects on source diversity and off-platform exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic curation has been found to increase source diversity in some respects while simultaneously reducing the number of external links presented to users, which limits exposure to off-platform content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure both on-platform source/topic diversity and external-link exposure. A system can score well on internal diversity while still isolating users from outside sources—both dimensions matter for informational robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of echo chambers and filter bubbles
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms recommend content the system predicts a user will engage with positively; content from accounts with differing perspectives is less likely to be surfaced, which may reduce source and topic diversity and contribute to the formation of echo chambers and filter bubbles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate propensity to reinforce existing viewpoints: quantify exposure to differing perspectives, assess personalization strength, and consider user control features. Watch for user-side narrowing (blocking/muting) that compounds algorithmic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration / over-representation of visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A pattern observed is the concentration of algorithmic visibility among a small subset of users: content from the most active users, those with the largest followings, or those generating the most engagement tends to be surfaced more frequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess distribution of impressions/engagement across accounts (Gini-like concentration metrics). Consider whether algorithmic amplification favors incumbents and how that affects plurality of voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal dynamics and interaction effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Research using agent-based modelling has examined how user behaviour, information quality, and algorithmic design interact with one another over time; algorithmic curation changes users' feeds over time through these interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should include longitudinal/dynamic analyses (not only snapshot metrics): feedback loops, amplification over time, and whether design choices lead to stable or divergent informational ecosystems. Agent-based and simulation studies are recommended to probe long-term effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cold-start / first-time user handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For first-time users without prior history, personalized search may draw on content-based filtering to establish an initial context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess strategies for users with little/no history (e.g., default recommendations, content-based seeding), and evaluate whether those strategies introduce biases or limit exposure. Robust cold-start design reduces initial personalization errors.
